name: Lee Carr
episode: The worker who couldn't read the joke
life: “I still remember starting my break early so the room would be empty.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Lee by a small Wednesday habit. Lee can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I used to avoid the break room. We are holding one lunch where people can explain what actually makes them laugh.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. Lee has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Lee looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Lee treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Lee lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To hold one shared lunch with jokes everyone understands.
family: Cecil Hooper is Lee’s cousin raised in the same household. Lee gets to change the plan. Cecil offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Two left slippers*, Cecil says, “I can deliver to the whole ward in my lunch hour if somebody will lend me a bicycle.”
connections: Amos Choi. A misunderstood home word gives the lunch organizer a starting point for the next meal.

reactions.situation: A manager wants the photographed worker to address the crew
reactions.response: Lee offers the pictured worker a private conversation before any meeting with the crew.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Lee lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.
